summary: Columns that line up across rows, with gaps from the spacing scale. Reach for it before writing grid CSS: cards and tiles, a main column beside its aside, a form in two columns.
useWhen: things that should line up in columns across rows — cards, tiles, a set of settings
a main column beside a narrower aside that falls under it on a smaller screen
a form's short fields side by side, one above the other on a phone

useInstead.when: things one after another in a single column or along a single line
useInstead.why: a Stack has no columns to keep in line, and a row of controls sizes each to its content

useInstead.when: a set of numbers with their labels at the top of a dashboard
useInstead.why: it lays its tiles out and names the group for a screen reader

useInstead.when: a label beside its value, row after row
useInstead.why: it is a `dl`: a screen reader hears each term with its value

composition.note: `columns` is a count of equal columns (`3`) or each column's share of the row (`[2, 1]`: a main column twice its aside); it defaults to 2. Fixed columns fall to one at `collapse`: `mobile` (767px and below, the default), `tablet` (1023px and below — for a main column and its aside), or `never` (a pair that fits a phone, like two short numbers). `minColumnWidth` (160–360) instead fills each row with as many equal columns as fit, so a set of cards needs no breakpoint at all. `gap` is a step of the spacing scale, 16 by default; `rowGap` sets the rows apart when they need more. Cells in a row stretch to the tallest by default, so cards line up at the bottom too; `align="start"` lets each keep its height. Pass `as="ul"` for a list of cards and give each an `li`. Every column is `minmax(0, …)`, so a wide child — a table, a long ID — scrolls inside its cell rather than widening the page.

mobile.use: the default — columns that read fine on a tablet: a form's fields in two columns, three small cards

tablet.use: a main column and its aside, or columns that need a desktop's width to hold what is in them

never.use: columns narrow enough for a phone — two short numbers, a pair of small toggles

children.note: one cell each, in reading order across then down; `li` children when `as` is `ul` or `ol`

guarantees: layout only: it adds no role, so the element given by `as` — or the children — carry the meaning
the visual order is the DOM order: cells are placed across then down, never moved by `order` or explicit placement
no column can push the page sideways: every track is `minmax(0, …)`, and a filling grid's minimum gives way to a screen narrower than it
`as="ul"` stays a list to a screen reader while losing its bullets
requires: `as` for a group that means something — a list of cards is a `ul` — rather than a div
notes: It renders on a server. A gap off the spacing scale, a column count it does not offer and a minimum width off its steps are type errors, not styles.

antiPatterns.dont: a hand-written `display: grid` with a pixel gap and its own media query
antiPatterns.why: the gap drifts off the scale and the breakpoint off the tokens', and nothing catches either

antiPatterns.dont: fixed columns for a set of cards whose count varies
antiPatterns.why: the columns then follow the space: three on a desktop, one on a phone, with no breakpoint to choose

antiPatterns.dont: `collapse="never"` on columns that hold text or tables
antiPatterns.why: on a phone each column is a sliver; the words wrap one to a line and a table scrolls in a strip
a single column is a Stack; the Grid only adds a template nothing uses
